text.p: nStor Technologies Inc said it has a definitive agreement to acquire the business -- assets and liabilities -- of Parity Systems Inc for $2.8 million cash, plus a warrant to purchase 500,000 nStor common shares at $2.10 per share.

Parity had sales of $32 million in 1995 and is "on pace to do $28 to $30 million" this year, nStor President Mark Levy said Tuesday. This year's decline is due to a shortage of new disc drives, he explained.

The company said the warrant exercise price is based on the market price on the date of execution of the previously-announced letter of intent regarding the acquisition of the privately-owned integrator of storage management solutions, digital media management, and client/server systems for RISC-based UNIX and Windows NT Server environments headquartered in Los Gatos, Calif.
nStor stock was trading at 2-9/16 early Tuesday afternoon, off 2/16 from Monday's close. The company said it has 18,660,477 common shares outstanding.
Closing of the transaction is expected to occur by December 31 and is subject to certain conditions, including completion of due diligence, nStore said.

"We expect to begin transitioning our technology to their product line over the coming year, and by combining compatible operations we should realize significant operating efficiencies, while lowering our component sourcing cost," nStor said.
The company said its nStor Corp subsidiary, which will be acquiring Parity, generated sales of about $5.6 million during its first five months of operation, ended October 31.

"We estimate that annualized revenues from the combined nStor and Parity operations will exceed $40 million," nStor said. Results for nStor's fourth quarter and year ended October 31 should be reported in early January, it said.
The company has said it plans to change to a December 31st fiscal year end and will report operating results for the November-December 1996 period separately.
